claims.text: CSRF: attacker tricks browser into making a request to the target site from a malicious site
claims.quote: In a cross-site request forgery (CSRF) attack, an attacker tricks the user or the browser into making an HTTP request to the target site from a malicious site.

claims.text: The request carries the user's credentials and the server thinks the user intended it
claims.quote: The request includes the user's credentials and causes the server to carry out some harmful action, thinking that the user intended it.

claims.text: SameSite controls cookies in cross-site requests, three values
claims.quote: This attribute controls when a browser is allowed to include the cookie in a cross-site request.

claims.text: Strict: cookie is not sent in any cross-site request
claims.quote: The Strict value offers the most protection: if this attribute is set, the browser will not include the cookie in any cross-site request.

claims.text: SameSite gives some protection against CSRF
claims.quote: The SameSite cookie attribute provides some protection against CSRF attacks.
